dish.title: Okonomiyaki (Japanese Cabbage Pancakes)

recipe_version.title: Okonomiyaki (Japanese Cabbage Pancakes)
recipe_version.description: Thick, crisp-edged cabbage-and-scallion pancakes with seared shiitake on the underside, brushed with a quick homemade okonomi-style sauce (ketchup, Worcestershire, soy), striped with Japanese egg-yolk mayonnaise, and showered with bonito flakes. No pork, shrimp, squid, or cheese.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: 2/3 cup. Plain water stands in for dashi: dashi powders such as Hondashi commonly contain lactose (milk), so no dashi powder is used in this package.

ingredients.name: soy sauce
ingredients.note: divided: 1 tsp in the batter, 2 tsp in the sauce. Soy and wheat.

ingredients.name: green cabbage
ingredients.preparation: cored and very finely shredded (1/8 inch), about 6 packed cups

ingredients.name: scallions
ingredients.preparation: thinly sliced; greens of 2 reserved for garnish

ingredients.name: shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.note: stand in for the traditional pork-belly layer

ingredients.name: neutral high-heat oil
ingredients.note: 1 1/2 tbsp per batch. Not peanut oil.

ingredients.name: Worcestershire sauce
ingredients.note: HARD CONTRACT: classic anchovy-based Worcestershire (vinegar, molasses, anchovies, tamarind, spices). Contains finfish (anchovy). No oyster or other shellfish ingredient. Malt vinegar may contain barley.

ingredients.name: Japanese mayonnaise
ingredients.note: HARD CONTRACT: egg-yolk mayonnaise (oil, egg yolk, vinegar, salt, seasoning). Mayonnaise is egg-based and contains no milk. Do not substitute a 'creamy' dressing or mayo-style spread that lists milk, buttermilk, or cheese. Egg allergen.

ingredients.name: bonito flakes
ingredients.note: loosely packed, about 5 g. Plain dried, smoked skipjack tuna shavings, not a dashi seasoning blend. Finfish.

steps.title: Shred the cabbage and make the sauce
steps.body: Core the cabbage and shred it very finely (about 1/8 inch) to get 6 packed cups. Thinly slice the scallions and set aside the greens of 2 for garnish. Stem the shiitake and thinly slice the caps. For the okonomi-style sauce, whisk 1/4 cup ketchup, 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 2 tsp of the soy sauce, and 2 tsp sugar until the sugar dissolves. Spoon the Japanese mayonnaise into a small zip-top bag (snip a tiny corner later) or a squeeze bottle. Contract check: no pork belly, no shrimp, no squid, no tenkasu, no cheese, no dashi powder. About 12 minutes.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.body: In a large bowl whisk the 1 cup flour, 1/2 tsp baking powder, and 1/2 tsp kosher salt. Add the 2/3 cup cold water, the remaining 1 tsp soy sauce, and the 4 eggs and whisk until smooth. Fold in the cabbage and the sliced scallions (not the reserved greens) until every shred is coated. The mixture should be mostly cabbage, just bound by batter. About 3 minutes.

steps.title: Heat the skillet
steps.body: Set a 12-inch nonstick skillet (or an electric griddle at 375 F) over medium heat with 1 1/2 tbsp of the neutral oil until shimmering. About 2 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the first side of batch one
steps.body: Scoop a quarter of the batter into each side of the pan to form two rounds about 5 1/2 inches wide and 3/4 inch thick; tidy the edges with the spatula. Lay a quarter of the shiitake slices over the top of each, pressing them in lightly. Cover and cook until the underside is deep golden and the edges look set, 4 to 5 minutes. About 5 minutes.

steps.title: Flip and finish batch one
steps.body: Using two wide spatulas, flip each pancake so the mushrooms are on the bottom. Press gently, cover, and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the mushrooms are browned and the center is set: a thin knife in the middle comes out with no wet batter (the egg batter should reach 160 F). Flip once more so the first golden side faces up and move to a plate or rack, loosely tented. About 5 minutes.

steps.title: Cook batch two
steps.body: Add the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp oil and repeat the two-sided cook with the rest of the batter and shiitake: 4 to 5 minutes covered, flip, 4 to 5 minutes covered, flip back. About 11 minutes.

steps.title: Sauce, mayo, and bonito
steps.body: With the golden side up, spoon or brush the okonomi sauce over each pancake right to the edges. Snip a small corner of the mayo bag and pipe thin parallel lines across, then drag a chopstick through at right angles for a lattice. Scatter the bonito flakes (they ripple in the heat) and the reserved scallion greens; add aonori and pickled red ginger if using. Cut into wedges and serve hot. About 3 minutes. kitchen_tested is false.

components.name: quick okonomi-style sauce
components.contract: Made in the recipe instead of bottled okonomi sauce, which can contain oyster extract (shellfish).

components.name: Japanese mayo lattice, bonito flakes, scallion greens
components.contract: Mayonnaise is egg-yolk mayonnaise with no milk; bonito flakes are plain katsuobushi.

equipment: 12-inch nonstick skillet with lid (or electric griddle with a cover)
recipe_version.time_clock: Prep 15 = 12 shred/slice/sauce + 3 batter. Cook 26 = 2 heat pan + 5 first side + 5 flip and finish (batch one) + 11 batch two + 3 dress. Two pancakes per batch, two batches. No oven.
recipe_version.heat: Stovetop medium (or griddle 375 F), covered for each side so the thick cabbage center steams through while the outside crisps. No oven.
recipe_version.doneness: Both faces deep golden and crisp at the edges; center set with no wet batter (about 160 F for the egg batter); cabbage tender-crisp; shiitake browned. kitchen_tested is false.

dietary_eligibility.nut_policy_note: No peanuts, tree nuts, or cashews. Frying oil is contracted canola or grapeseed, not peanut oil.
dietary_eligibility.hh001_reason: Finfish (bonito flakes; anchovy in the Worcestershire) and eggs (batter, egg-yolk mayonnaise) are allowed for HH001. No pork belly, shrimp, squid, or other meat/shellfish. No dairy: the mayonnaise is contracted egg-yolk mayo with no milk, no cheese is used, and dashi powder (which commonly contains lactose) is deliberately excluded. The okonomi sauce is made in the recipe to avoid bottled sauces with oyster extract. No nuts.

recipe_version.dietary_label_note: Unconditional dairy_free: no milk, butter, cheese, or cream; mayonnaise is egg-based by contract; no dashi powder (lactose risk) by design. Not vegetarian (bonito flakes and anchovy-based Worcestershire are fish).
allergen_notes: Wheat covers the flour and the soy sauce. Worcestershire malt vinegar may also contain barley (gluten, not a separate token).
Egg covers the 4 eggs in the batter and the egg-yolk mayonnaise.
Finfish covers the bonito flakes (skipjack tuna) and the anchovies in classic Worcestershire.
Soy covers the soy sauce (batter and sauce) and is commonly present in Japanese mayonnaise oil.
No milk, sesame, peanut, tree_nut, shellfish, meat, or poultry. Optional aonori (seaweed) and pickled ginger add no tokens.
recipe_version.hh001_reason: Finfish (bonito flakes; anchovy in the Worcestershire) and eggs (batter, egg-yolk mayonnaise) are allowed for HH001. No pork belly, shrimp, squid, or other meat/shellfish. No dairy: the mayonnaise is contracted egg-yolk mayo with no milk, no cheese is used, and dashi powder (which commonly contains lactose) is deliberately excluded. The okonomi sauce is made in the recipe to avoid bottled sauces with oyster extract. No nuts.
